text: Types of networks that use a particular version of Wi-Fi. That's why their standard name is actually similar to that that I pointed out to be possible versions of Wi-Fi. I abbreviated to dot in a because they use a particular version of Wi-Fi. But they are very peculiar. Think of users that, for example, are stationary users living in one of these buildings. Each building has got a Wi-Fi access point and router that is connected with other access points and routers located in nearby buildings. And then only few of them are actually connected with the internet. So in this picture, the red markers here are those access points and routers that are directly communicated with the internet. The blue ones, instead, are those that communicate with each other, and some of them communicate also with the red ones. So mesh network, they are called mesh networks because when you have many nodes connected to each other, that's a mesh topology. So.
